raw: Act 1, Scene 1 — A public place

sentences.en: A public place

summary.en: Two families, the Montagues and the Capulets, hate each other. Their servants start a street fight, and the Prince warns everyone. Romeo is sad because Rosaline does not love him.
summary.ko: 몬태규 가문과 캐퓰릿 가문은 서로 미워한다. 두 집안의 하인들이 거리에서 싸움을 일으키고, 영주가 모두에게 경고한다. 로미오는 로잘린이 자신을 사랑하지 않아 슬퍼한다.

raw: Enter Chorus.

speaker: CHORUS
raw:
Two households, both alike in dignity,
In fair Verona, where we lay our scene,
From ancient grudge break to new mutiny,
Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.
From forth the fatal loins of these two foes
A pair of star-cross’d lovers take their life;
Whose misadventur’d piteous overthrows
Doth with their death bury their parents’ strife.
The fearful passage of their death-mark’d love,
And the continuance of their parents’ rage,
Which, but their children’s end, nought could remove,
Is now the two hours’ traffic of our stage;
The which, if you with patient ears attend,
What here shall miss, our toil shall strive to mend.

sentences.en: Two families, both equally respected, live in lovely Verona, where our play takes place.
sentences.ko: 우리 극의 무대인 아름다운 베로나에, 똑같이 존경받는 두 가문이 살고 있습니다.

sentences.en: An old hatred between them breaks out into new fighting.
sentences.ko: 그들 사이의 오랜 증오가 새로운 싸움으로 터져 나옵니다.

sentences.en: Citizens' blood makes citizens' hands dirty.
From these two enemy families, two unlucky lovers are born.
sentences.ko: 원수인 이 두 가문에서 불운한 연인 한 쌍이 태어납니다.

sentences.en: The stars are against them.
Their sad, unlucky deaths finally bury their parents' fight.
sentences.ko: 그들의 슬프고 불운한 죽음이 마침내 부모들의 싸움을 묻어 버립니다.

sentences.en: Their doomed love and their parents' endless anger are our story.
sentences.ko: 그들의 비극적인 사랑과 부모들의 끝없는 분노가 우리의 이야기입니다.

sentences.en: We will show it on our stage for the next two hours.
sentences.ko: 앞으로 두 시간 동안 이 무대에서 그 이야기를 보여 드리겠습니다.

sentences.en: Only their children's deaths could end that anger.
sentences.ko: 자식들의 죽음만이 그 분노를 끝낼 수 있었습니다.

sentences.en: If you listen patiently, we will work hard to fix anything we get wrong.
sentences.ko: 참을성 있게 들어 주신다면, 부족한 점은 열심히 채우겠습니다.

raw: Exit.
Enter Sampson and Gregory armed with swords and bucklers.

sentences.en: Sampson and Gregory enter with swords and shields.
sentences.ko: 샘슨과 그레고리가 칼과 방패를 들고 등장한다.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Gregory, on my word, we’ll not carry coals.

sentences.en: Gregory, I promise we will not put up with insults.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: No, for then we should be colliers.

sentences.en: No, because then we would be coal sellers.
sentences.ko: 아니, 그러면 우린 석탄 장수가 되는 거잖아.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: I mean, if we be in choler, we’ll draw.

sentences.en: I mean, if we are angry, we will fight.
sentences.ko: 내 말은, 화가 나면 싸우겠다는 뜻이야.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: Ay, while you live, draw your neck out o’ the collar.

sentences.en: Yes, while you live, pull your neck out of the collar.
sentences.ko: 그래, 살아 있는 동안 목이 밧줄에 걸리지 않게 조심해.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: I strike quickly, being moved.

sentences.en: I strike quickly when I am moved.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: But thou art not quickly moved to strike.

sentences.en: But you are not quickly moved to strike.
sentences.ko: 하지만 넌 그렇게 빨리 움직이지 않잖아.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: A dog of the house of Montague moves me.

sentences.en: A dog from the house of Montague makes me move.
sentences.ko: 몬태규 집안 개 한 마리만 봐도 나는 움직여.

speaker: GREGORY
raw:
To move is to stir; and to be valiant is to stand: therefore, if thou
art moved, thou runn’st away.

sentences.en: To move means to stir.
To be brave is to stand your ground.
If you are moved, it means you run away.
sentences.ko: 네가 움직인다는 건 겁을 먹고 도망친다는 뜻이고.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
A dog of that house shall move me to stand.
I will take the wall of any man or maid of Montague’s.

sentences.en: A dog of that house will make me stand.
sentences.ko: 그 집안 개라면 나를 버티고 서게 만들지.

sentences.en: I will push any Montague man or woman off the wall side of the street.
sentences.ko: 몬태규 가문 남자든 여자든 길가 벽 쪽으로 밀어버릴 거야.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: That shows thee a weak slave, for the weakest goes to the wall.

sentences.en: That makes you look like a weak slave.
sentences.ko: 그건 네가 약한 노예라는 걸 보여 주는 거야.

sentences.en: The weakest person is always pushed to the wall.
sentences.ko: 제일 약한 놈이 항상 벽으로 밀려나는 법이야.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
True, and therefore women, being the weaker vessels, are ever thrust to
the wall: therefore I will push Montague’s men from the wall, and
thrust his maids to the wall.

sentences.en: That is true.
Women are weaker, so they are always pushed to the wall.
sentences.ko: 여자는 약하니까 항상 벽 쪽으로 밀려나지.

sentences.en: Therefore, I will push Montague's men away from the wall.
sentences.ko: 그러니 몬태규 가문 남자들은 벽에서 멀리 밀어버릴 거야.

sentences.en: I will push his maids to the wall.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: The quarrel is between our masters and us their men.

sentences.en: The fight is only between our masters and us, their men.
sentences.ko: 싸움은 우리 주인들, 그리고 우리 하인들끼리의 일이야.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
’Tis all one, I will show myself a tyrant: when I have fought with the
men I will be civil with the maids, I will cut off their heads.

sentences.en: It is all the same.
I will act like a tyrant.
When I have fought with the men, I will be polite to the maids.
sentences.ko: 남자들과 싸운 뒤에는 하녀들에게 예의를 갖춰줄게.

sentences.en: I will cut off their heads.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: The heads of the maids?

sentences.en: The heads of the maids?

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
Ay, the heads of the maids, or their maidenheads; take it in what sense
thou wilt.

sentences.en: Yes, the heads of the maids.
Or their virginity.
Take it in whatever sense you want.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: They must take it in sense that feel it.

sentences.en: They must take it in the sense that they feel it.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
Me they shall feel while I am able to stand: and ’tis known I am a
pretty piece of flesh.

sentences.en: They will feel me while I am able to stand.
sentences.ko: 내가 서 있는 동안 사람들은 나를 주목할 거야.

sentences.en: It is known that I am a handsome piece of flesh.
sentences.ko: 내 몸이 아주 멋지다는 건 누구나 아는 사실이지.

speaker: GREGORY
raw:
’Tis well thou art not fish; if thou hadst, thou hadst been poor John.
Draw thy tool; here comes of the house of Montagues.

sentences.en: It is good that you are not a fish.
If you were a fish, you would be a dried, salted fish.
Draw your weapon.
Here come some men from the house of Montagues.

raw: Enter Abram and Balthasar.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: My naked weapon is out: quarrel, I will back thee.

sentences.en: My naked weapon is out.
Start a fight, and I will back you up.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: How? Turn thy back and run?

sentences.en: How?
Will you turn your back and run?

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Fear me not.

sentences.en: Do not fear me.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: No, marry; I fear thee!

sentences.en: No way!
I am so scared of you!

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Let us take the law of our sides; let them begin.

sentences.en: Let us keep the law on our side.
Let them start first.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: I will frown as I pass by, and let them take it as they list.

sentences.en: I will frown as I walk past.
They can take it however they want.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw:
Nay, as they dare. I will bite my thumb at them, which is disgrace to
them if they bear it.

sentences.en: No, if they dare.
I will bite my thumb at them.
sentences.ko: 난 그들에게 엄지손가락을 깨물어 보일 거야.

sentences.en: It is an insult to them if they accept it.

speaker: ABRAM
raw: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

sentences.en: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: I do bite my thumb, sir.

sentences.en: I do bite my thumb, sir.

speaker: ABRAM
raw: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

sentences.en: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Is the law of our side if I say ay?

sentences.en: Is the law on our side if I say yes?
sentences.ko: 내가 그렇다고 하면 법이 우리 편이 될까?

speaker: GREGORY
raw: No.

sentences.en: No.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: No sir, I do not bite my thumb at you, sir; but I bite my thumb, sir.

sentences.en: No sir.
I do not bite my thumb at you, sir.
sentences.ko: 너를 보고 엄지손가락을 깨문 게 아니야.

sentences.en: But I bite my thumb, sir.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: Do you quarrel, sir?

sentences.en: Do you quarrel, sir?

speaker: ABRAM
raw: Quarrel, sir? No, sir.

sentences.en: Quarrel, sir?
No, sir.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: But if you do, sir, I am for you. I serve as good a man as you.

sentences.en: But if you do, sir, I am for you.
I serve as good a master as you do.

speaker: ABRAM
raw: No better.

sentences.en: No better.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Well, sir.

sentences.en: Well, sir.

raw: Enter Benvolio.

speaker: GREGORY
raw: Say better; here comes one of my master’s kinsmen.

sentences.en: Say better.
One of my master's relatives is coming here.
sentences.ko: 내 주인의 친척 중 한 명이 여기 오고 있어.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Yes, better, sir.

sentences.en: Yes, better, sir.

speaker: ABRAM
raw: You lie.

sentences.en: You are lying.

speaker: SAMPSON
raw: Draw, if you be men. Gregory, remember thy washing blow.

sentences.en: Draw your weapons if you are men.
Gregory, remember to hit him hard.

raw: They fight.

sentences.en: They fight.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Part, fools! put up your swords, you know not what you do.

sentences.en: Stop it, fools!
Put away your swords.
You do not know what you are doing.
sentences.ko: 너희가 무슨 짓을 하는지 모르고 있구나.

raw: Beats down their swords.

sentences.en: Benvolio beats down their swords.

raw: Enter Tybalt.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
What, art thou drawn among these heartless hinds?
Turn thee Benvolio, look upon thy death.

sentences.en: What, have you drawn your sword among these cowardly servants?
sentences.ko: 뭐야, 이 겁쟁이 하인들 사이에서 칼을 뽑아든 거야?

sentences.en: Turn around, Benvolio.
Look at your death.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
I do but keep the peace, put up thy sword,
Or manage it to part these men with me.

sentences.en: I am only trying to keep the peace.
Put away your sword.
Or use it to separate these men with me.
sentences.ko: 아니면 그 칼로 나와 함께 이 사람들을 떼어놓든가.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
What, drawn, and talk of peace? I hate the word
As I hate hell, all Montagues, and thee:
Have at thee, coward.

sentences.en: You have your sword out, and you talk of peace?
I hate that word as much as I hate hell.
I hate all Montagues and I hate you.
sentences.ko: 난 모든 몬태규를 증오하고 너도 증오해.

sentences.en: Fight me, coward.

raw: They fight.

sentences.en: They fight.

raw: Enter three or four Citizens with clubs.

sentences.en: Three or four citizens enter with clubs.
sentences.ko: 몽둥이를 든 시민 세네 명이 들어온다.

speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
raw:
Clubs, bills and partisans! Strike! Beat them down!
Down with the Capulets! Down with the Montagues!

sentences.en: Get clubs and spears and strike!
Beat them down!
Down with the Capulets and down with the Montagues!

raw: Enter Capulet in his gown, and Lady Capulet.

sentences.en: Capulet enters in his gown.
Lady Capulet enters.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: What noise is this? Give me my long sword, ho!

sentences.en: What noise is this?
Give me my long sword!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: A crutch, a crutch! Why call you for a sword?

sentences.en: A crutch, a crutch!
Why do you call for a sword?

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
My sword, I say! Old Montague is come,
And flourishes his blade in spite of me.

sentences.en: My sword, I say!
Old Montague has come.
He waves his blade in spite of me.
sentences.ko: 그자가 날 약 올리려고 칼을 휘두르고 있어.

raw: Enter Montague and his Lady Montague.

sentences.en: Montague and Lady Montague enter.

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw: Thou villain Capulet! Hold me not, let me go.

sentences.en: You villain Capulet, do not hold me and let me go.
sentences.ko: 이 악당 캐퓰릿! 날 붙잡지 마, 놓으라고.

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
raw: Thou shalt not stir one foot to seek a foe.

sentences.en: You shall not move one foot to look for an enemy.
sentences.ko: 적을 찾으러 한 발짝도 움직이면 안 돼요.

raw: Enter Prince Escalus, with Attendants.

sentences.en: Prince Escalus enters with his attendants.

speaker: PRINCE
raw:
Rebellious subjects, enemies to peace,
Profaners of this neighbour-stained steel,—
Will they not hear? What, ho! You men, you beasts,
That quench the fire of your pernicious rage
With purple fountains issuing from your veins,
On pain of torture, from those bloody hands
Throw your mistemper’d weapons to the ground
And hear the sentence of your moved prince.
Three civil brawls, bred of an airy word,
By thee, old Capulet, and Montague,
Have thrice disturb’d the quiet of our streets,
And made Verona’s ancient citizens
Cast by their grave beseeming ornaments,
To wield old partisans, in hands as old,
Canker’d with peace, to part your canker’d hate.
If ever you disturb our streets again,
Your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.
For this time all the rest depart away:
You, Capulet, shall go along with me,
And Montague, come you this afternoon,
To know our farther pleasure in this case,
To old Free-town, our common judgement-place.
Once more, on pain of death, all men depart.

sentences.en: You are rebellious subjects.
You are enemies of peace.
You stain your steel in this fight.
Will you not listen?
You men, you beasts!
You put out the fire of your harmful rage with purple fountains coming from your veins.
sentences.ko: 너희는 혈관에서 뿜어져 나오는 보랏빛 분수로 파괴적인 분노를 끄고 있다.

sentences.en: Under pain of torture, throw your angry weapons to the ground.
sentences.ko: 고문을 당하기 싫거든 성난 무기를 땅에 던져라.

sentences.en: Listen to the sentence of your prince.
Old Capulet and Montague, a careless word from you has started three street fights.
sentences.ko: 늙은 캐퓰릿과 몬태규, 너희의 부주의한 말 한마디가 세 건의 거리 싸움을 불러일으켰다.

sentences.en: They have broken the peace of our streets.
They have made Verona's old citizens put aside their dignified clothes.
sentences.ko: 그들 때문에 베로나의 노인들이 품위 있는 옷을 벗어 던져야 했다.

sentences.en: They had to pick up old spears, rusty from years of peace, to stop your poisonous hatred.
sentences.ko: 너희의 독 같은 증오를 막기 위해 그들은 오랜 평화로 녹슨 옛 창을 집어 들어야만 했다.

sentences.en: If you ever disturb our streets again, your lives will be the price for the peace.
sentences.ko: 다시 거리를 어지럽힌다면, 평화를 깬 대가로 너희 목숨을 내놓게 될 것이다.

sentences.en: Now, everyone else leave.
You, Capulet, will go with me.
And Montague, come this afternoon to hear my decision in this case.
sentences.ko: 몬태규, 오늘 오후에 내 결정을 들으러 오너라.

sentences.en: Come to old Free-town, our court of judgment.
sentences.ko: 우리의 재판소가 있는 옛 프리타운으로 오너라.

sentences.en: Once more, under pain of death, everyone leave.
sentences.ko: 다시 말하노니, 죽고 싶지 않거든 모두 물러가라.

raw: Exeunt Prince and Attendants; Capulet, Lady Capulet, Tybalt, Citizens and Servants.

sentences.en: Prince and his attendants leave.
Capulet, Lady Capulet, Tybalt, citizens, and servants also leave.
sentences.ko: 캐퓰릿, 캐퓰릿 부인, 티볼트, 시민들, 그리고 하인들도 모두 떠난다.

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw:
Who set this ancient quarrel new abroach?
Speak, nephew, were you by when it began?

sentences.en: Who started this old fight again?
sentences.ko: 누가 이 오래된 싸움을 다시 시작했느냐?

sentences.en: Speak, nephew; were you here when it began?
sentences.ko: 말해 보거라, 조카야. 싸움이 시작될 때 여기 있었느냐?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Here were the servants of your adversary
And yours, close fighting ere I did approach.
I drew to part them, in the instant came
The fiery Tybalt, with his sword prepar’d,
Which, as he breath’d defiance to my ears,
He swung about his head, and cut the winds,
Who nothing hurt withal, hiss’d him in scorn.
While we were interchanging thrusts and blows
Came more and more, and fought on part and part,
Till the Prince came, who parted either part.

sentences.en: The servants of your enemy and yours were here.
sentences.ko: 숙부님 댁 하인들과 적의 하인들이 여기 있었어요.

sentences.en: They were fighting closely before I came near.
sentences.ko: 제가 다가가기 전부터 그들은 맞붙어 싸우고 있었어요.

sentences.en: I stepped in to separate them.
In that moment, the angry Tybalt came.
He had his sword ready.
As he shouted defiance at my ears, he swung it over his head and cut the air.
sentences.ko: 그는 제 귀에 대고 도전의 말을 외치며, 머리 위로 칼을 휘둘러 공기를 갈랐어요.

sentences.en: The wind was not hurt by it.
sentences.ko: 바람은 그 칼에 상처를 입지 않았고요.

sentences.en: The wind hissed at him in scorn.
While we were trading hits and blows, more people came and fought on different sides.
sentences.ko: 우리가 서로 치고받는 동안, 더 많은 사람들이 몰려와 각자 다른 쪽에서 싸웠어요.

sentences.en: Until the Prince came and separated both sides.

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
raw:
O where is Romeo, saw you him today?
Right glad I am he was not at this fray.

sentences.en: Where is Romeo?
Did you see him today?
I am very glad he was not at this fight.
sentences.ko: 그가 이 싸움에 없었다니 정말 다행이야.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Madam, an hour before the worshipp’d sun
Peer’d forth the golden window of the east,
A troubled mind drave me to walk abroad,
Where underneath the grove of sycamore
That westward rooteth from this city side,
So early walking did I see your son.
Towards him I made, but he was ware of me,
And stole into the covert of the wood.
I, measuring his affections by my own,
Which then most sought where most might not be found,
Being one too many by my weary self,
Pursu’d my humour, not pursuing his,
And gladly shunn’d who gladly fled from me.

sentences.en: Madam, it was an hour before the sun rose in the golden window of the east.
sentences.ko: 숙모님, 동쪽의 황금빛 창문으로 해가 뜨기 한 시간 전이었어요.

sentences.en: A troubled mind forced me to walk outside.
sentences.ko: 불안한 마음 때문에 밖을 걸어 다니게 되었고요.

sentences.en: I walked under the grove of sycamore trees.
Those trees grow toward the west from this side of the city.
sentences.ko: 그 숲은 도시 이쪽에서 서쪽으로 뻗어 있어요.

sentences.en: I saw your son walking very early.
sentences.ko: 아주 이른 새벽에 숙모님의 아드님이 걷는 것을 보았어요.

sentences.en: I moved toward him, but he noticed me.
He hid in the thick part of the woods.
I measured his feelings by my own feelings.
sentences.ko: 저는 제 기분에 비추어 그의 마음을 짐작했어요.

sentences.en: I wanted to be where no one could find me.
sentences.ko: 저는 아무도 찾지 못할 곳에 있고 싶었거든요.

sentences.en: Even my own company was too much for me.
I followed my own mood instead of following his.
sentences.ko: 저는 그를 따라가지 않고 제 기분을 따랐어요.

sentences.en: I happily avoided him, and he gladly fled from me.
sentences.ko: 저는 기꺼이 그를 피했고, 그도 기꺼이 저를 피해 달아났어요.

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw:
Many a morning hath he there been seen,
With tears augmenting the fresh morning’s dew,
Adding to clouds more clouds with his deep sighs;
But all so soon as the all-cheering sun
Should in the farthest east begin to draw
The shady curtains from Aurora’s bed,
Away from light steals home my heavy son,
And private in his chamber pens himself,
Shuts up his windows, locks fair daylight out
And makes himself an artificial night.
Black and portentous must this humour prove,
Unless good counsel may the cause remove.

sentences.en: He has been seen there many mornings.
sentences.ko: 그는 많은 아침에 그곳에서 목격되곤 했다.

sentences.en: His tears added to the fresh morning dew.
His deep sighs added more clouds to the sky.
sentences.ko: 그의 깊은 한숨은 하늘에 구름을 더 얹었지.

sentences.en: But the cheerful sun soon begins to open the curtains of the morning.
sentences.ko: 하지만 밝은 태양은 곧 아침의 커튼을 열기 시작한다.

sentences.en: Then my sad son leaves the light and goes home.
sentences.ko: 그러면 내 슬픈 아들은 빛을 떠나 집으로 돌아간다.

sentences.en: He stays in his room alone.
He shuts his windows and locks out the daylight.
He makes himself an artificial night.
sentences.ko: 그는 스스로를 가짜 밤 속에 가둔다.

sentences.en: This mood will lead to something dark and bad, unless good advice can remove its cause.
sentences.ko: 좋은 조언이 그 원인을 없애주지 않는다면, 이 기분은 어둡고 나쁜 일로 이어질 것이다.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?

sentences.en: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw: I neither know it nor can learn of him.

sentences.en: I do not know it and I cannot learn from him.
sentences.ko: 나는 모르고 그에게 물어볼 수도 없어.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Have you importun’d him by any means?

sentences.en: Have you tried to talk to him in any way?

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw:
Both by myself and many other friends;
But he, his own affections’ counsellor,
Is to himself—I will not say how true—
But to himself so secret and so close,
So far from sounding and discovery,
As is the bud bit with an envious worm
Ere he can spread his sweet leaves to the air,
Or dedicate his beauty to the sun.
Could we but learn from whence his sorrows grow,
We would as willingly give cure as know.

sentences.en: Both I and many other friends have tried.
sentences.ko: 나를 포함한 많은 친구가 시도해 봤어.

sentences.en: But he is the only counselor of his own feelings.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그 애는 자기 마음을 혼자서만 의논하는 아이야.

sentences.en: He is very private to himself, and I will not say how true it is.
sentences.ko: 그 애는 자기 속을 드러내지 않아. 얼마나 그러는지는 말도 못 할 정도지.

sentences.en: He is so secret and so close to himself.
He is far from sharing his thoughts or being discovered.
sentences.ko: 생각을 나누거나 남에게 들키는 걸 싫어해.

sentences.en: He is like a bud bitten by an envious worm.
sentences.ko: 그는 질투심 많은 벌레에게 물린 꽃봉오리 같아.

sentences.en: It dies before it can open its sweet leaves to the air.
sentences.ko: 달콤한 잎을 공기 중에 펼치기도 전에 시들어버리지.

sentences.en: Or show its beauty to the sun.
If only we could learn why he is sad!
sentences.ko: 그가 왜 슬퍼하는지 알 수만 있다면!

sentences.en: We would cure him as gladly as we would learn the cause.
sentences.ko: 원인을 알아내는 것만큼이나 기쁘게 그를 고쳐줄 텐데.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
See, where he comes. So please you step aside;
I’ll know his grievance or be much denied.

sentences.en: Look, here he comes.
Please step aside.
I will find out what is wrong, unless he flatly refuses to tell me.
sentences.ko: 그가 단호하게 거절하지 않는다면 제가 무슨 문제가 있는지 알아낼게요.

speaker: MONTAGUE
raw:
I would thou wert so happy by thy stay
To hear true shrift. Come, madam, let’s away,

sentences.en: I wish you luck in staying to hear the truth from him.
sentences.ko: 네가 그 애에게서 진실을 듣기를 바란다.

sentences.en: Come, madam, let us go.

raw: Exeunt Montague and Lady Montague.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Good morrow, cousin.

sentences.en: Good morning, cousin.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Is the day so young?

sentences.en: Is the day so young?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: But new struck nine.

sentences.en: It is only nine o'clock.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Ay me, sad hours seem long.
Was that my father that went hence so fast?

sentences.en: Oh, sad hours seem long.
Was that my father who left so quickly?
sentences.ko: 그렇게 빨리 떠난 사람이 내 아버지였나?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: It was. What sadness lengthens Romeo’s hours?

sentences.en: It was.
What sadness makes Romeo's hours feel long?
sentences.ko: 무슨 슬픔이 로미오의 시간을 이토록 길게 느끼게 하는 거지?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Not having that which, having, makes them short.

sentences.en: I do not have the thing that makes time pass quickly.
sentences.ko: 시간을 빨리 가게 할 무언가가 내겐 없어.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: In love?

sentences.en: In love?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Out.

sentences.en: Out.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Of love?

sentences.en: Out of love?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Out of her favour where I am in love.

sentences.en: I am out of favor with the woman I love.
sentences.ko: 내가 사랑하는 여인의 마음 밖에 있어.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Alas that love so gentle in his view,
Should be so tyrannous and rough in proof.

sentences.en: Love looks so gentle.
It is sad that it is so cruel and rough in real life.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Alas that love, whose view is muffled still,
Should, without eyes, see pathways to his will!
Where shall we dine? O me! What fray was here?
Yet tell me not, for I have heard it all.
Here’s much to do with hate, but more with love:
Why, then, O brawling love! O loving hate!
O anything, of nothing first create!
O heavy lightness! serious vanity!
Misshapen chaos of well-seeming forms!
Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire, sick health!
Still-waking sleep, that is not what it is!
This love feel I, that feel no love in this.
Dost thou not laugh?

sentences.en: It is sad that love is blindfolded, yet it can still find its way to what it wants!
sentences.ko: 사랑은 눈이 가려져 있는데도 원하는 곳은 잘도 찾아가니 슬픈 일이야!

sentences.en: Where shall we eat?
Oh me!
What fight was here?
Do not tell me, for I have heard it all.
There is much to do with hate, but there is even more to do with love.
sentences.ko: 증오에 관한 일도 많지만, 사랑에 관한 일은 훨씬 더 많아.

sentences.en: Why, then, oh fighting love!
Oh loving hate!
Oh anything created from nothing!
sentences.ko: 오 아무것도 없는 데서 태어난 모든 것이여!

sentences.en: Oh heavy lightness!
Serious vanity!
A misshapen chaos of beautiful forms!
A feather of lead.
Bright smoke.
Cold fire.
Sick health!
A sleep that stays awake.
It is not what it seems!
I feel this love, but I feel no love in this.
sentences.ko: 이 사랑을 느끼지만, 이 안에서 사랑은 느껴지지 않아.

sentences.en: Do you not laugh?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: No coz, I rather weep.

sentences.en: No friend, I would rather cry.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Good heart, at what?

sentences.en: Good heart, at what?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: At thy good heart’s oppression.

sentences.en: At your good heart's suffering.
sentences.ko: 네 착한 마음이 겪는 고통 때문이지.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Why such is love’s transgression.
Griefs of mine own lie heavy in my breast,
Which thou wilt propagate to have it prest
With more of thine. This love that thou hast shown
Doth add more grief to too much of mine own.
Love is a smoke made with the fume of sighs;
Being purg’d, a fire sparkling in lovers’ eyes;
Being vex’d, a sea nourish’d with lovers’ tears:
What is it else? A madness most discreet,
A choking gall, and a preserving sweet.
Farewell, my coz.

sentences.en: That is how love breaks the rules.
My own sorrows weigh heavily in my chest.
sentences.ko: 내 슬픔이 가슴 속에 무겁게 짓누르고 있어.

sentences.en: You will add your own sadness to them and make them heavier.
sentences.ko: 네가 네 슬픔을 더하면 내 슬픔은 더 무거워질 거야.

sentences.en: But the love you have shown adds more grief to my many problems.
sentences.ko: 하지만 네가 보여준 사랑은 나의 수많은 문제에 비탄을 더할 뿐이야.

sentences.en: Love is a smoke made from the smoke of sighs.
When it is clear, it is a fire sparkling in lovers' eyes.
sentences.ko: 그것이 선명해지면 연인들의 눈 속에서 반짝이는 불꽃이 되지.

sentences.en: When it is troubled, it is a sea fed by lovers' tears.
sentences.ko: 그것이 요동치면 연인들의 눈물로 채워지는 바다가 돼.

sentences.en: What else is it?
It is a very careful madness.
It is a bitter poison and a preserving sweetness.
Goodbye, my friend.

raw: Going.

sentences.en: Romeo starts to leave.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Soft! I will go along:
And if you leave me so, you do me wrong.

sentences.en: Wait!
I will go with you.
If you leave me alone, you do me wrong.
sentences.ko: 네가 나를 혼자 두고 가면, 내게 잘못을 저지르는 거야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Tut! I have lost myself; I am not here.
This is not Romeo, he’s some other where.

sentences.en: Tut! I have lost myself and I am not here.
sentences.ko: 쳇! 난 넋이 나갔어. 난 여기 없어.

sentences.en: This is not Romeo, he is somewhere else.
sentences.ko: 이건 로미오가 아니야, 그는 다른 곳에 있어.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Tell me in sadness who is that you love?

sentences.en: Tell me seriously, who do you love?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What, shall I groan and tell thee?

sentences.en: What, should I groan and tell you?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Groan! Why, no; but sadly tell me who.

sentences.en: Groan? No.
But tell me seriously who it is.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Bid a sick man in sadness make his will,
A word ill urg’d to one that is so ill.
In sadness, cousin, I do love a woman.

sentences.en: You are asking a sick man to seriously make his will.
sentences.ko: 병든 사람에게 유언을 남기라고 진지하게 묻는구나.

sentences.en: That is a cruel thing to say to someone so ill.
Seriously, cousin, I love a woman.
sentences.ko: 진심으로 말하자면, 사촌아, 난 한 여자를 사랑해.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: I aim’d so near when I suppos’d you lov’d.

sentences.en: I guessed correctly when I thought you were in love.
sentences.ko: 네가 사랑에 빠졌다고 생각했을 때 내 예상이 맞았군.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: A right good markman, and she’s fair I love.

sentences.en: You are a very good shot.
And the woman I love is beautiful.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: A right fair mark, fair coz, is soonest hit.

sentences.en: A beautiful target is the easiest to hit, my friend.
sentences.ko: 내 친구야, 아름다운 목표물은 맞히기가 가장 쉽단다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Well, in that hit you miss: she’ll not be hit
With Cupid’s arrow, she hath Dian’s wit;
And in strong proof of chastity well arm’d,
From love’s weak childish bow she lives uncharm’d.
She will not stay the siege of loving terms
Nor bide th’encounter of assailing eyes,
Nor ope her lap to saint-seducing gold:
O she’s rich in beauty, only poor
That when she dies, with beauty dies her store.

sentences.en: Actually, you missed that point because she will not be hit by Cupid's arrow.
sentences.ko: 사실 네 말은 틀렸어. 그녀는 큐피드의 화살에 맞지 않거든.

sentences.en: She thinks like Diana, the goddess who never falls in love.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 절대 사랑에 빠지지 않는 여신 디아나처럼 생각하니까.

sentences.en: She is well protected to keep her purity and is not affected by the weak arrows of love.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 순결을 지키기 위해 잘 보호받고 있어서, 약한 사랑의 화살이 통하지 않아.

sentences.en: She will not give in to romantic words or look at men who stare at her with desire.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 로맨틱한 말이나 자신을 갈망하는 눈빛으로 바라보는 남자들에게도 흔들리지 않아.

sentences.en: She will not give herself to a man's gold.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 남자의 황금에 자신을 팔지도 않아.

sentences.en: She is very rich in beauty.
However, she is poor because her beauty will disappear when she dies.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그녀는 가난해. 죽으면 그 아름다움도 함께 사라지니까.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Then she hath sworn that she will still live chaste?

sentences.en: So she has promised to stay pure forever?
sentences.ko: 그럼 그녀가 영원히 순결을 지키겠다고 약속한 거야?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
She hath, and in that sparing makes huge waste;
For beauty starv’d with her severity,
Cuts beauty off from all posterity.
She is too fair, too wise; wisely too fair,
To merit bliss by making me despair.
She hath forsworn to love, and in that vow
Do I live dead, that live to tell it now.

sentences.en: She has made that promise.
But her strictness wastes her beauty.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그 엄격함이 그녀의 아름다움을 낭비하게 만들지.

sentences.en: Her behavior stops her beauty from being passed on to the next generation.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 행동은 그녀의 아름다움이 다음 세대로 이어지는 것을 막아.

sentences.en: She is too beautiful and too wise to win heaven by making me miserable.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 너무 아름답고 현명해서, 나를 불행하게 하며 천국을 얻으려 해.

sentences.en: She has promised not to love anyone.
Because of that promise, I feel like a dead man.
sentences.ko: 그 약속 때문에 나는 죽은 사람처럼 느껴져.

sentences.en: I am alive only to tell people about my pain.
sentences.ko: 나는 그저 내 고통을 사람들에게 알리기 위해 살아있을 뿐이야.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Be rul’d by me, forget to think of her.

sentences.en: Listen to me.
Forget about her.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O teach me how I should forget to think.

sentences.en: Then teach me how to forget to think of her.
sentences.ko: 그녀를 잊고 생각하지 않는 법을 가르쳐줘.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
By giving liberty unto thine eyes;
Examine other beauties.

sentences.en: Let your eyes look freely.
Look at other beautiful women.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
’Tis the way
To call hers, exquisite, in question more.
These happy masks that kiss fair ladies’ brows,
Being black, puts us in mind they hide the fair;
He that is strucken blind cannot forget
The precious treasure of his eyesight lost.
Show me a mistress that is passing fair,
What doth her beauty serve but as a note
Where I may read who pass’d that passing fair?
Farewell, thou canst not teach me to forget.

sentences.en: That would only make me think more about how beautiful she is.
sentences.ko: 그건 그녀가 얼마나 아름다운지 더 생각나게 할 뿐이야.

sentences.en: These happy masks kiss the foreheads of beautiful ladies.
sentences.ko: 이 화려한 가면들이 아름다운 여인들의 이마에 닿아.

sentences.en: The masks are black.
They remind us that they hide something beautiful.
sentences.ko: 그것들은 무언가 아름다운 것을 숨기고 있다는 걸 상기시켜 주지.

sentences.en: A man who is struck blind cannot forget the precious treasure of his lost sight.
sentences.ko: 눈이 먼 사람은 잃어버린 시력이라는 소중한 보물을 잊을 수 없어.

sentences.en: Show me a woman who is very beautiful.
sentences.ko: 정말 아름다운 여자를 한 명 보여줘 봐.

sentences.en: Her beauty would only remind me of the woman who is even more beautiful.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 아름다움은 훨씬 더 아름다운 여자를 떠올리게 할 뿐이야.

sentences.en: Goodbye, you cannot teach me how to forget.
sentences.ko: 안녕, 넌 내가 잊는 법을 가르쳐줄 수 없어.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: I’ll pay that doctrine, or else die in debt.

sentences.en: I will teach you that lesson, or die trying.
sentences.ko: 그 가르침을 꼭 해 주겠어, 못 하면 죽어도 좋아.

raw: Exeunt.
